subject: Quick update on the setup
text: I finally had time to test the router again after my earlier message, and I think the connection problem was mostly a placement issue. When I moved it off the floor and away from the radiator, the signal became much steadier in the side room. If you do the same at the new place, try keeping it above table height and away from large metal shelves, because those things interfere more than people expect. Also, if your landlord gave you a starter kit, don't assume the username and password are printed on the modem sticker; sometimes they are on the paperwork inside the bag. I'd jot them down on your phone now before you move everything. I also checked the old notes you asked about, and the tenant portal sometimes lags when there is a building maintenance notice, so an error message does not always mean the request was lost. If you want to be safe, send the same note through the secondary contact form and save the receipt. The neighbor upstairs mentioned he had trouble with the same thing last spring, and it cleared once someone from maintenance manually acknowledged the request. I would wait one business day before calling, unless the problem stops you from logging in entirely. If the installation crew is coming Friday, have the confirmation email open and maybe take a photo of the outlet behind the desk, since a power adapter missing can delay things for twenty minutes. One last thing: if the old apartment wifi keeps dropping after you move out, you can usually disconnect it from your saved networks instead of resetting everything. Hope this saves you a call later—let me know if it still acts up.
